short_description: Balanced late-war Sherman with a 75 mm gun, wet stowage, and strong machine-gun support. Reliable, flexible, and well suited to infantry support and general armored combat.
long_description: A dependable American medium tank that trades raw anti-armor power for versatility. Its 75 mm gun handles soft targets well, the MG suite is strong, and its armor and mobility are solid without being exceptional.

short_description: Late-war Sherman with HVSS suspension and a 76 mm gun. Smoother ride, better anti-tank punch, and good all-around handling make it a strong general-purpose armor unit.
long_description: The Easy Eight keeps the Sherman formula but sharpens it for late-war combat. Better suspension helps mobility over rough ground, while the 76 mm gun gives it a much better chance against heavier armor.

short_description: Open-topped tank destroyer armed with a hard-hitting 3-inch gun. Good reach and mobility, but thin armor and exposed crew make it vulnerable in a close fight.
long_description: Built to hunt enemy armor rather than trade blows like a tank. The M10 is effective when positioned well, but its open turret and lighter protection punish careless play.

short_description: Extremely fast open-topped tank destroyer with a 76 mm gun. Best used for flanking, rapid redeployment, and ambushes rather than standing toe to toe with heavier vehicles.
long_description: One of the fastest armored vehicles of the war. The Hellcat lives on speed and initiative, striking from favorable angles before its light armor and exposed turret can be punished.

short_description: Open-topped tank destroyer mounting a powerful 90 mm gun. Strong anti-armor reach with decent mobility, but still vulnerable to artillery, MG fire, and close assault.
long_description: The M36 brings heavyweight gun power to the American tank destroyer line. It can threaten dangerous targets at range, but its open fighting compartment keeps it from being a true heavy brawler.

short_description: British Sherman conversion carrying the fearsome 17-pounder. Excellent anti-tank performance on a familiar chassis, with the usual Sherman strengths and compromises.
long_description: A practical answer to heavier German armor. The Firefly keeps the Sherman’s mobility and usability while replacing the main gun with a much more dangerous anti-tank weapon.

short_description: Workhorse German medium tank with the long 75 mm gun. Good anti-tank performance, decent frontal protection, and broad utility across many battlefield roles.
long_description: The Panzer IV H is a solid, flexible battlefield tank rather than a specialist. Its gun remains dangerous, but side armor and overall survivability are less forgiving than heavier German designs.

short_description: Fast, hard-hitting German tank with excellent frontal armor and a superb long 75 mm gun. Strong at range, but less comfortable when flanked or forced into awkward close terrain.
long_description: The Panther combines high velocity firepower with dangerous frontal protection. It excels in open fights and long sight lines, but side shots and mechanical strain remain real concerns.

short_description: Heavy tank with thick armor and the famous 88 mm gun. A dominant direct-fire threat, especially from prepared positions, though size and cost make every loss painful.
long_description: The Tiger is built to win head-on engagements through armor and gun power. It can overmatch many opponents, but it is expensive, conspicuous, and never easy to replace.

short_description: Low-profile assault gun with a strong long 75 mm and solid frontal armor. Efficient, dangerous, and best when fighting from cover or prepared lines rather than scouting ahead.
long_description: The StuG III G is a compact gun platform that rewards disciplined positioning. It lacks a full turret, but its low silhouette and efficient firepower make it deadly in defensive combat.

short_description: Towed 75 mm anti-tank gun with strong penetration and a very low profile. Excellent in ambushes and defensive lines, but vulnerable once spotted or forced to move.
long_description: The Pak 40 is one of the core German anti-tank weapons of the war. It is dangerous and efficient when dug in, but towing, setup, and crew exposure make mobility its weak point.

short_description: Heavy dual-purpose gun effective against aircraft and armored targets. Powerful, long-ranged, and deadly with support, but large, visible, and dependent on crew and setup.
long_description: The 88 is as much a battlefield system as a single gun. It reaches high and hits hard, serving as both flak and anti-tank weapon, but its size and deployment demands make concealment harder.

short_description: Armored half-track for moving infantry under light protection, usually backed by MG 34 fire. Useful for mobility and escort work, but not a front-line dueling vehicle.
long_description: The Sd.Kfz. 251 gets troops and support weapons forward faster than foot movement alone. It can contribute suppressive fire, but thin armor means it should avoid serious anti-armor threats.

short_description: Standard cargo truck for transport, towing, and general logistics. Fast on roads and useful for support work, but completely unsuited to direct combat once enemy fire starts.
long_description: The Opel Blitz is a backbone logistics vehicle rather than a fighting platform. It moves men and supplies efficiently, but even light battlefield threats can disable or destroy it quickly.
